text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — ran a set of queueing sims for continuous batching to compare pure FIFO with backpressure vs adding soft priority lanes. Uploading CSV and a short summary. Need engineering take on safe defaults and preemption costs. <http://perf.internal/sim/17695>
maria: Can you paste the top-line numbers here? Hard to parse CSV on my phone.
alex: Top-lines: FIFO under short-request heavy tail (p95/p99) -> 95ms / 420ms. Soft-priority lanes (2 lanes: short/long) -> 95ms / 290ms. Preemption-enabled -> 95ms / 210ms but increased CPU sys% and dropped overall batch efficiency ~8%.
sam: Interesting. So preemption helps tail but hurts batching efficiency. Do we have per-model or per-client breakdowns?
alex: Yes, short requests are mostly a single-token or <50 token distribution from conversational endpoints. Long ones are 200-2k tokens. Per-client: enterprise folks have a lot of short fanout traffic, so priority lanes favor them and reduce their tail.
jen: Starvation risk for low-priority is a concern. Did you observe unbounded queue growth for long lane under heavy load?
alex: With naive soft lanes and strict priority, yes — the long lane queue grows until we hit droprate. With fairness window + soft quota (we experimented with token-bucket style lambda), the long lane stabilized but p99 for long requests jumped.
ci-bot: simulation run 1769504320 completed in 13m 42s — artifacts: /artifacts/sim-17695.tar.gz
maria: What configs did you try? names and defaults please (so we can align with the console knobs).
alex: Config snippet we used:
```
queueing:
  lane_count: 2
  lane_policy:
    short: { priority: 10, preempt: true, min_batch: 4 }
    long:  { priority: 1, preempt: false, min_batch: 8 }
  preempt_threshold_ms: 40
  preempt_budget_ms: 60
  max_queue_size: 5000
```
sam: Preempt threshold 40ms — is that time-in-queue or expected service time?
alex: Time-in-queue. If short request waits >40ms and there's a long running batch starting, it can preempt the long batch if preempt_budget allows.
jen: How are you implementing preemption? cancel running GPU kernel and reconstruct KV cache? That seems expensive.
alex: We simulated preemption as: stop accepting new tokens for the long batch, flush outputs we have, move remaining requests back to queue and schedule short batch immediately. In practice that costs ~1.2x GPU work because of wasted kernel op and cache churn.
maria: That matches our concerns. Maybe prefer admission control + small dedicated fast path for tiny requests (size-based fastlane) instead of preemption.
sam: What about bucketing by token-length prior to batching? i.e., separate small-window coalescing to avoid fragmentation. That keeps batch quality and avoids preempt.
alex: We tried length bucketing too. Pros: batches are homogeneous, higher kernel efficiency. Cons: adds more queues -> head-of-line blocking risk if some buckets are starved. Also adds extra sharding complexity for multi-tenant fairness.
jen: Could we combine approaches: length buckets + a small shared emergency lane with preemption only for SLO breaches? So preemption is gated and rare.
alex: That's what one sim looked like: 3 lanes {fast, normal, emergency}, preempt only from emergency and with preempt_budget_ms=30. Tail improved and wasted work reduced vs naive preempt. Cost delta ~+3% vs FIFO.
ci-bot: note: sim config and raw traces in artifact: sim-17695/traces/*
maria: Any impact on embedding / KV cache hit rates? fragmentation could reduce reuse right?
alex: Good call — KV cache reuse drops ~12% when we aggressively preempt because we reshuffle sequence ids and rewarm cache. Length bucketing preserves cache locality better.
sam: For a rollout path, I'd prefer conservative defaults: lane_count=3, preempt_budget_ms=30, min_batch_short=4, min_batch_long=12, fairness_window_s=60. Gradually enable preempt for specific clients.
jen: Also require SLA guardrails: if a tenant has p95 > threshold for >2m, trigger temporary dedicated lane or rate-limit non-critical traffic.
alex: Agree. I'll draft RFC update with those defaults and include simulation artifacts and a small test harness. Plan: A/B on a small subset of pods, monitor p95/p99, batch efficiency, and cache-reuse metric. If cost deltas >5% revert.
maria: One more ask — include a simple backpressure knob exposed in console: `max_queue_depth_per_lane` + `fallthrough_to_cpu` toggle. Ops wants visible control.
alex: Will add that. Also adding rollout playbook: how to revert if long-request QoE regresses.
sam: Command I used to reproduce sim locally:
```
./bin/sim --config sim-17695.yaml --workload short-heavy --out results.json
```
jen: Thanks. @alex please cc @eng-sre and @product when you post RFC update so we can align on SLO and pricing implication.
alex: Will do. Drafting now — aiming to have RFC + appendix with sim configs by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
